title: Rule 7 must validate lossless IPv6/UDP match constraints before compression
description: Security review finding: spec/03-adaptation.md Rule 7 now says the rule matches a UDP packet whenever either endpoint port is 10883, but it no longer states the complete lossless matching and validation preconditions. A compressor that elides/recomputes fields without validating them can normalize nonzero IPv6 Traffic Class or Flow Label, inconsistent IPv6 Payload Length or UDP Length, a non-UDP Next Header, or a zero/invalid UDP checksum into a different valid packet on decompression. This launders malformed or corrupted input across a hop and creates implementation divergence. The normative Rule 7 definition must enumerate IPv6 version=6, Traffic Class=0, Flow Label=0, Next Header=UDP, endpoint-port matching, consistent IPv6/UDP lengths, and a valid mandatory IPv6 UDP checksum. Packets that fail must be dropped or use Rule 255 without semantic normalization.
acceptance_criteria: The normative Rule 7 text contains the full IPv6/UDP matching and input-validation constraints and defines drop versus Rule-255 fallback. Canonical cross-implementation negative vectors cover nonzero Traffic Class, nonzero Flow Label, non-UDP Next Header, IPv6 payload-length mismatch, UDP-length mismatch, zero checksum, and bad checksum. Rust, Zephyr/C, and Python reject or fall back identically, while every accepted packet round-trips byte-for-byte except fields explicitly and validly recomputed by the profile. The compressor validates the original IPv6 UDP checksum before eliding it; the decoder recomputes and installs a checksum rather than claiming to validate an unavailable original. A shared vector forces a mathematical zero checksum result and all implementations encode it canonically as 0xffff, never UDP zero.
notes:
Additional interoperability/security acceptance: specify the canonical IPv6 UDP checksum representation when one's-complement checksum arithmetic produces numeric zero. The transmitted checksum MUST be 0xffff, never 0x0000; Rule 7 compression validation and decompression must agree on that mapping. Add a deliberately constructed checksum-zero payload vector and verify Rust, Zephyr/C, and Python all serialize/validate 0xffff identically while rejecting a zero wire checksum.
Correctness pass detail: Rule 7 elides the original UDP checksum, so a decoder cannot validate the sender checksum after decompression; only the compressor can validate the original. The decoder must recompute and install the checksum. If the ones-complement computation yields mathematical zero, IPv6 UDP requires transmitting 0xffff rather than zero. The current phrase validate the computed nonzero checksum is tautological and should be replaced with explicit recomputation/installation behavior.
